name: CSD201 — Luyện tập Cấu trúc dữ liệu & Giải thuật bằng Java (chạy & tự chấm trên máy)
description: Bộ luyện môn CSD201 (Data Structures and Algorithms, Java) theo từng bài học: độ phức tạp, mảng động, danh sách liên kết đơn/vòng/kép, ngăn xếp, hàng đợi, hàng đợi ưu tiên, đệ quy, cây nhị phân, BST, AVL, heap, đồ thị (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, cây khung nhỏ nhất, Euler), sắp xếp, băm, xử lý văn bản (KMP, Huffman, LZW, RLE), ⭐ thuật toán phỏng vấn và đề PE đúng khuôn trường (MyList/BSTree/Graph đọc data.txt, ghi f1.txt…). Website KHÔNG chấm: mỗi đề tải về một thư mục (code khởi đầu + máy chấm cham.mjs + ca mẫu), bạn làm trên máy với JDK của mình rồi chạy "node cham.mjs" — nó biên dịch bằng javac --release 8, chạy nhiều ca (có ca ẩn), so output từng dòng có diff, đi theo đúng các liên kết head/next/prev/left/right của cấu trúc bạn dựng (reflection), đo độ phức tạp trên input lớn có hạn giờ rồi cho điểm; đạt hết thì bấm "Tự đánh dấu đã giải".

modules.name: 0.3 Big-O: the language of efficiency
modules.description: Luyện: arrayMax: count the primitive operations · Count without counting: closed forms for seven loops · Linear vs binary search: count the probes, then search a million times

modules.name: 0.5 🧪 Practice — complexity in code: prefix sums, duplicates, doubling, a PE-style CarList
modules.description: Luyện: Prefix sums: answer 200,000 range-sum queries · Find a duplicate in O(n): from all pairs to a HashSet · A flexible array that doubles: amortized O(1) append · CarList f1–f4 on an array: max, range count, stable sort, binary search

modules.name: 1.1 Arrays & dynamic arrays
modules.description: Luyện: MyArrayList: insert and remove at an index by shifting · Remove every occurrence in one pass (two indexes) · Rotate an array by k in place: three reversals

modules.name: 1.2 Singly, circular & doubly linked lists
modules.description: Luyện: Singly linked list: addFirst, addLast in O(1), removeFirst, removeLast · insertAt(k, x) and deleteAt(k) on a singly linked list · A circular list with only a tail: add, remove, rotate in O(1) · Doubly linked list: O(1) at both ends, links checked both ways

modules.name: 1.3 Doubly linked lists with sentinels
modules.description: Luyện: Header and trailer sentinels: every operation through addBetween and remove · A sorted doubly linked list with sentinels: insertSorted and removeAll · Browser history on a doubly linked list: visit, back, forward

modules.name: 1.4 Java in practice: ArrayList vs LinkedList
modules.description: Luyện: Remove while iterating: Iterator.remove on any List · Merge two sorted Lists with iterators, whatever their class · Pick the right structure: a ticket queue of 400,000 customers

modules.name: 1.5 Three classic list problems: reverse, cycle, merge
modules.description: Luyện: Reverse a singly linked list in place — the same nodes, no recursion · Floyd’s tortoise and hare: find where the cycle starts, in O(1) memory · Merge two sorted linked lists by relinking — not one new node

modules.name: 1.6 🧪 Practice — Josephus, palindrome list and a 🎯 PE-format MyList paper
modules.description: Luyện: The Josephus circle on a circular linked list · Is the linked list a palindrome? O(n) time, O(1) memory, list restored · 🎯 PE format — MyList of Cars: f1 addLast with a condition, f2 insert as 3rd, f3 delete the first max, f4 stable sort

modules.name: 2.1 Stacks (LIFO) & Queues (FIFO)
modules.description: Luyện: A linked stack: push, pop, top — all at the head · A linked queue: enqueue at the tail, dequeue at the head, both O(1) · Reverse the first k elements of a queue with a stack

modules.name: 2.2 Implementing stacks & queues: circular array vs linked
modules.description: Luyện: An array stack that grows correctly (and the off-by-one in top) · Circular array queue with first/last as on the slides — wrap around, then grow in queue order · A queue made of two stacks: amortized O(1)

modules.name: 2.3 Stack applications: brackets, RPN, undo
modules.description: Luyện: Balanced brackets — and where the first error is · Evaluate a postfix (RPN) expression · Infix to postfix with the shunting-yard algorithm · Undo and redo with two stacks

modules.name: 2.4 Deques & the sliding-window maximum
modules.description: Luyện: A deque on a circular array: add and remove at both ends in O(1) · Sliding window maximum in O(n) with a monotonic deque · First negative number in every window of size k

modules.name: 2.5 Priority Queues & Heaps
modules.description: Luyện: A priority queue on a binary min-heap: insert and removeMin in O(log n) · The k largest of a million numbers with a heap of size k · Emergency triage: severity first, then arrival order, with a Comparator

modules.name: 2.6 🧪 Practice — round-robin, a patient queue (PE), monotonic stacks
modules.description: Luyện: A round-robin CPU scheduler with a queue · PE style: a patient priority queue on a sorted linked list (f1–f4) · Next greater element with a monotonic stack · Largest rectangle in a histogram (stack, O(n))

modules.name: 3.1 Recursion & the call stack
modules.description: Luyện: Sum, count and maximum of an array — recursively · Reverse a string and test a palindrome — recursively · Decimal to any base from 2 to 16 — the digits come out on the way back

modules.name: 3.2 The four classic recursions
modules.description: Luyện: Towers of Hanoi: the moves, and how many there are · Fibonacci: from exponential to linear with memoization · Fast power: aⁿ mod m with O(log n) multiplications

modules.name: 3.3 Analysing recursion: recursion trees & the Master theorem
modules.description: Luyện: How many calls does naive fib(n) make? Solve the recurrence, do not run it · Count inversions in O(n log n) — merge sort with a counter · Maximum subarray by divide and conquer (best crossing the middle)

modules.name: 3.4 Designing recursion & eliminating tail calls
modules.description: Luyện: Eliminate the tail call: three tail-recursive functions become loops · Flood fill with an explicit stack: regions of a 2000 × 2000 map · A recursive-descent calculator: expression → term → factor

modules.name: 3.5 🧪 Practice — list recursion, backtracking, N queens, memoized grid paths
modules.description: Luyện: PE style: count, sum, max and print backwards on a linked list — recursively · Backtracking: subsets with a given sum, and permutations in order · N queens: count every placement and print the first one · Grid paths with obstacles: recursion + memo instead of 10¹⁶ calls

modules.name: 4.1 Trees & traversals
modules.description: Luyện: A general tree: size, height and the depth of a node · Disk usage of a folder tree: a postorder traversal · Print a general tree level by level (breadth-first)

modules.name: 4.2 Binary trees: properties & two implementations
modules.description: Luyện: Properties of a linked binary tree: size, height, leaves, full and perfect · A binary tree in an array: parent, children, depth, and "is it complete?" · Rebuild a binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals

modules.name: 4.3 The four traversals & expression trees
modules.description: Luyện: The four traversals of a binary tree: preorder, inorder, postorder, level order · Inorder without recursion — on a degenerate tree of a million nodes · Expression trees: build from postfix, print infix, evaluate

modules.name: 4.4 Binary Search Trees
modules.description: Luyện: BST insert (no duplicates) and search — iteratively · Floor, ceiling and counting keys in a range — with pruning · Is this binary tree a BST? Check every node against its bounds

modules.name: 4.5 BST insertion & the three deletion cases
modules.description: Luyện: Delete by copying: the predecessor takes the place · Delete by merging: hang the right subtree under the predecessor · Trim a BST to [lo, hi] — a recursion that returns the new subtree

modules.name: 4.6 AVL trees: the four rotations
modules.description: Luyện: Rotate a node right or left — and keep its parent linked · AVL insertion: the four cases LL, RR, LR, RL · Balance factors: is it an AVL tree, and which node breaks it?

modules.name: 4.7 Building a heap: sift-up, sift-down, Floyd
modules.description: Luyện: Build a max-heap two ways: top-down (insertions) and bottom-up (Floyd) · Heap sort in place, O(n log n) guaranteed · Merge k sorted arrays with a heap of k cursors

modules.name: 4.8 🧪 Practice — BST statistics, k-th smallest & LCA, and a 🎯 PE-format BSTree paper
modules.description: Luyện: PE style: leaves, one-child nodes, height, a price range and the maximum of a BST · k-th smallest key and the lowest common ancestor in a BST · 🎯 PE format — BSTree of Cars: f1 insert + breadth/inorder, f2 filtered preorder, f3 delete by copying, f4 rotate right

modules.name: 5.1 Graph representation & traversal
modules.description: Luyện: Degrees, edges, isolated and odd vertices from an adjacency matrix · Breadth-first and depth-first traversal that reaches every vertex · Connected components: how many, which vertices, is it connected?

modules.name: 5.2 Three ways to store a graph
modules.description: Luyện: From an edge list to an adjacency matrix and adjacency lists (directed or not) · A million vertices: BFS on adjacency lists (a matrix would need 4 TB) · Count walks of length k with powers of the adjacency matrix

modules.name: 5.3 DFS: cycles, components, topological order
modules.description: Luyện: Directed cycle detection and a topological order from DFS finishing times · Kahn’s algorithm: the smallest available course first · Component sizes of a million-vertex graph with an iterative DFS

modules.name: 5.4 BFS & shortest paths in unweighted graphs
modules.description: Luyện: The path with the fewest edges, rebuilt from BFS parents · Shortest way out of a 2000 × 2000 maze · Multi-source BFS: distance from every house to the nearest hospital

modules.name: 5.5 Dijkstra step by step
modules.description: Luyện: PE style Dijkstra on a matrix: the path, its length and the order of the set S · Dijkstra with a PriorityQueue on 200,000 vertices and a million edges · The cheapest route across a grid of tolls (Dijkstra on cells)

modules.name: 5.6 Minimum spanning trees: Prim & Kruskal
modules.description: Luyện: Prim’s algorithm on a matrix: the edges in the order they are chosen · Kruskal with union-find: a million edges · Connect every city: some roads already exist (cost 0)

modules.name: 5.7 Euler tours, Euler cycles & Hamilton
modules.description: Luyện: Euler cycle, Euler path or neither? Degrees and connectivity · Find the Euler cycle: Hierholzer with an explicit stack · Hamilton cycles by backtracking: count them and print the first

modules.name: 5.8 🧪 Practice — sequential colouring, Floyd–Warshall, and a 🎯 PE-format Graph paper
modules.description: Luyện: Sequential colouring: natural order versus largest degree first · Floyd–Warshall: every pair, a negative edge, and the paths · 🎯 PE format — Graph: f1 depth-first from C with the degrees of the 2nd–6th vertices, f2 an Euler cycle from A

modules.name: 6.1 Basic sorts (O(n²))
modules.description: Luyện: Selection sort: the array after every pass, and the number of swaps · Insertion sort: passes, shifts — and why it is fast on almost sorted data · Bubble sort that stops early: count the passes it really needs

modules.name: 6.2 Efficient sorts: quick, merge, heap
modules.description: Luyện: Shell sort with Knuth’s gaps 1, 4, 13, 40, … · Sort cars by price (high to low), then by owner (A to Z) — with a Comparator · Sort first, then solve: the two closest numbers in O(n log n)

modules.name: 6.3 Quick-sort: partitioning in detail
modules.description: Luyện: Lomuto partition: the pivot’s final index and the array after each partition · A quick sort that survives sorted input: median of three, recurse on the smaller side · Quickselect: the k-th smallest without sorting everything

modules.name: 6.4 Merge-sort & stability
modules.description: Luyện: Top-down merge sort: every merge, in the order it happens · Bottom-up merge sort: no recursion, one buffer, two million values · Stability: sort student records by grade, keeping the name order

modules.name: 6.5 Heap-sort
modules.description: Luyện: Heap sort step by step: the heap after building, then after every extraction · Sort an almost sorted array (each value at most k places away) in O(n log k) · The running median with two heaps

modules.name: 6.6 Linear-time sorting: bucket & radix
modules.description: Luyện: Counting sort: stable, O(n + k), no comparisons · LSD radix sort, one digit per pass — the slides’ trace · Bucket sort for real numbers in [0, 1)

modules.name: 6.7 Choosing a sort: the full comparison
modules.description: Luyện: The Dutch national flag: sort 0s, 1s and 2s in one pass · The minimum number of swaps to sort a permutation (count the cycles) · Sort once, search many: a million membership queries

modules.name: 6.8 🧪 Practice — sorting linked lists of cars, PE style
modules.description: Luyện: Merge sort on a linked list of cars: price, then owner — O(n log n), no new nodes · PE style: sort only positions i..j of a linked list, descending by price · Insertion sort of a linked list by relinking nodes (stable)

modules.name: 7.1 Hash tables & collisions
modules.description: Luyện: Two values with sum K: one pass with a HashSet · Word frequencies with a HashMap, and the top k · Group anagrams with a HashMap keyed by the sorted letters

modules.name: 7.2 Hash functions & the hashCode/equals contract
modules.description: Luyện: Polynomial hashing by Horner’s rule — and counting collisions · Your own key class: equals and hashCode that agree · Rabin–Karp: find every occurrence with a rolling hash

modules.name: 7.3 Collision handling in depth
modules.description: Luyện: Linear probing with "deleted" marks: insert, search, delete · Quadratic probing with car plates: h, h+1, h+4, h+9, … · Separate chaining: one linked list per bucket

modules.name: 7.4 Load factor, rehashing & Java HashMap
modules.description: Luyện: A chained hash table that doubles when the load factor passes 0.75 · A bad hashCode turns HashMap into a list: fix the key class · An open-addressing int set that grows: no boxing, two million values

modules.name: 7.5 🧪 Practice — consecutive runs, subarray sums, a PE-style chained catalogue
modules.description: Luyện: The longest run of consecutive integers in O(n) · How many subarrays sum to K? Prefix sums in a HashMap · PE style: a book catalogue with separate chaining (f1–f4)

modules.name: 8.1 Compression: Huffman, LZW, RLE
modules.description: Luyện: RLE: encode, decode, and the compression rate of the slides · DNA in 2 bits per base: pack four bases into one byte · Is it a prefix code? Then decode a bit string with it

modules.name: 8.2 Pattern matching: brute force & KMP
modules.description: Luyện: The KMP table T[] of the slides, and every occurrence with the comparisons · KMP against brute force on two million characters · The shortest period of a string, read from the KMP table

modules.name: 8.3 Huffman coding, built step by step
modules.description: Luyện: Build the Huffman tree the slides’ way, then encode and decode · The total Huffman length without building codes: the sum of the merges · Entropy, average code length and compression rate of a text

modules.name: 8.4 LZW & RLE, encoded and decoded
modules.description: Luyện: LZW encoding with the slides’ numbering (codes start at 1) · LZW decoding — including the special case cW = the code being created · RLE for black-and-white images: alternating run lengths

modules.name: 8.5 🧪 Practice — brute force, a PE-style message log, choosing a compression
modules.description: Luyện: PE style: brute-force matching, every position and the number of comparisons · The message log (close to a real PE): f1 KMP search, f2 RLE, f3 Huffman bits · Which compression wins? RLE, LZW and Huffman on the same text

modules.name: 11.1 🎯 PE practice — the real papers SP26 Paper 1 and SP26 Block 5 Paper 4
modules.description: Luyện: 🎯 Real paper SP26 Paper 1 — ShipmentCLL (count, remove by id) + FruitBST (insert, count in a range) · 🎯 Real paper SP26 Block 5 Paper 4, Q1 — MyList of Drum: conditional addLast, insert as 3rd and 5th, delete after the first max, sort the last 4 · 🎯 Real paper SP26 Block 5 Paper 4, Q2 — BSTree of Tiger: insert by sound, filtered pre-order, delete by copying, rotate left · 🎯 Real paper SP26 Block 5 Paper 4, Q3 — Graph: part of a BFS order, Dijkstra paths and the last vertices added to S
